workflow_hints: protein bands were excised from the gel and the gel slices submitted to an in-gel trypsin digestion

Database search with Mascot were done using the following settings: a maximum of two trypsin miss cleavage allowed, methionine oxidation and protein N-terminus acetylation as variable modifications and cysteine carbamidomethylation as fixed modification.

Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a classic AP-MS (Affinity Purification Mass Spectrometry) using endogenous SLX4 immunoprecipitation. Quantification was performed using label-free methods (TIC and spectrum counting). Search parameters included N-terminal acetylation and methionine oxidation.

scope: Immunoprecipitation of overexpressed SLX4 coupled to mass spectrometry (IP-MS) analyses suggested that it associates with MutSβ, MutSα or both complexes.
Whole cell extracts from HeLa Flp-In T-Rex cells were used for immunoprecipitation performed with anti-SLX4 antibodies
After immunoprecipitation, protein complexes were analysed by LC-MSMS.
Immunoprecipitated protein complexes associated to SLX4 eluted from the beads with LDS sample buffer were loaded on NuPAGE 4-12% Bis-Tris acrylamide gels

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry was performed on material affinity-purified via immunoprecipitation of SLX4. While the starting material was whole cell extract, the analyzed material was the purified complex.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment described in the PRIDE metadata is an AP-MS study designed to identify interactors of endogenous SLX4. The primary biological comparison used to validate the interactome is the depletion of SLX4 via siRNA versus a non-targeting control (siLUC). While the main text describes various CRISPR-Cas9 cell lines and drug treatments (MMC, 6-TG, MNNG), these were used for functional assays (clonogenic survival, in vitro MMR) and not for the mass spectrometry analysis described in the PRIDE record.
